changes.title: Permission added: Work Orders — Move Labor
changes.after: exists; default ON for Admin, Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, Foreman, Parts Manager
changes.risk_reason: New permission granted by default to existing system roles — users gain access on upgrade.

codeComment.comment: SV-8911 — gates moving labor between WO lines. A WO sub-setting rather than a Work Order Lines CRUD level, because a shop must be able to grant line/labor editing without move-labor (the two were fused before).

plain.headline: New permission: Work Orders — Move Labor
plain.what: A new permission called “Work Orders — Move Labor” was added. It is switched on automatically for: Admin, Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, Foreman and Parts Manager.
plain.why: People with these roles get new access as soon as they move to this release.
check: Open a role in Administration › Roles and Permissions and check “Work Orders — Move Labor” is listed, in the right section, with the right name.
Log in as someone whose role has “Work Orders — Move Labor” and try it: it should work.
Log in as someone whose role does not have it and try it: it should be blocked, and the button or page should not be shown.
Check it is switched on for Admin, Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, Foreman and Parts Manager, and off for every other role.

qa_scenarios: Role editor: "Work Orders — Move Labor" appears in the right section with the right label, OFF for custom roles unless the template grants it.
Positive: a role WITH "Work Orders — Move Labor" can perform the action; negative: a role WITHOUT it cannot (UI hidden AND API 403).
Dependency: ticking "Work Orders — Move Labor" auto-ticks its required parents; unticking a parent clears it.
Defaults: check every system role holds or lacks it exactly as the change report lists.

changes.title: API guard changed: POST /api/work-orders/tasks/move
changes.risk_reason: The endpoint now checks something different.

plain.headline: Creating or running work orders › tasks › move: the permission check changed
plain.what: Creating or running work orders › tasks › move is now protected by a different permission check.
plain.why: The wrong people could be allowed in, or the right people blocked.
check: Log in as someone whose role has one of the permissions listed and try it: it should work.
Log in as someone whose role has none of them and try it: it should be blocked, and the button or page should not be shown.

qa_scenarios: API authorisation: call POST /api/work-orders/tasks/move as a role WITH and a role WITHOUT "Invoicing & Payments — Create & Edit" — expect 2xx and 403.
Front end: the matching screen action is shown only to roles the API allows (front end blocks + back end allows = pass; the reverse is a defect).
Cross-role: try the same call as each system role whose defaults include or exclude the permission.

changes.title: Dependency added: Work Orders — Move Labor ⇒ Work Order Lines — Create & Edit
changes.after: implies Work Order Lines — Create & Edit
changes.risk_reason: Granting the child now also grants (or requires) the parent.

plain.headline: Turning on “Work Orders — Move Labor” now also turns on “Work Order Lines — Create & Edit”
plain.what: When a role gets “Work Orders — Move Labor”, it also turns on “Work Order Lines — Create & Edit”. This happens automatically.
plain.why: Giving someone one permission now gives them another one as well.
check: Edit a role, tick “Work Orders — Move Labor”, and check “Work Order Lines — Create & Edit” is ticked too.
Untick “Work Order Lines — Create & Edit” and check “Work Orders — Move Labor” is unticked as well.

qa_scenarios: Role editor: ticking "Work Orders — Move Labor" now auto-ticks "Work Order Lines — Create & Edit".
API (bypassing the editor): create a role with only the child permission via the role API and confirm what the server stores.
Negative: unticking the parent clears the child.

changes.title: Role editor dependency logic changed (front end)
changes.risk_reason: The editor's auto-tick / confirm-dialog code changed (comments ignored). Re-test the editor cascades and confirmation dialogs.
changes.label: Role editor
workflows: Administration › Roles and Permissions › Create / Edit role

plain.headline: The role editor’s automatic ticking changed
plain.what: The part of the role editor that ticks and unticks related permissions for you was changed.
plain.why: Editing a role could now tick, untick or warn differently.
check: Open Administration › Roles and Permissions, edit a role, and tick permissions that depend on others. Check the related ones tick and untick as expected.
Turn off a permission that others depend on and check the warning message still appears.

qa_scenarios: Screens: open the screens listed and confirm controls tied to "Role editor" show/hide/disable correctly for a role with and without it.
Nav: top-level navigation items for the area appear only for roles holding the permission.

plain.headline: New protected action: Creating or running technician tasks › move
plain.what: There is a new action in the app (creating or running technician tasks › move). Only people with “Timesheets — Create & Edit” can use it.
plain.why: A new feature: make sure the right people can use it and nobody else can.
check: Log in as someone whose role has “Timesheets — Create & Edit” and try it: it should work.
Log in as someone whose role does not have it and try it: it should be blocked, and the button or page should not be shown.

qa_scenarios: API authorisation: call POST /api/technician-tasks/move as a role WITH and a role WITHOUT "Timesheets — Create & Edit" — expect 2xx and 403.
Front end: the matching screen action is shown only to roles the API allows (front end blocks + back end allows = pass; the reverse is a defect).
Cross-role: try the same call as each system role whose defaults include or exclude the permission.
